result.document_summary: California Civil Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just-cause eviction statute), as amended by AB 1529 effective January 1, 2026, operative April 1, 2024 and repealed January 1, 2030.
result.notes: One just-cause eviction rule extracted as the statewide regime. The section yields to local just-cause ordinances adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 or more protective ordinances adopted later. Subdivision (m) states the section became operative April 1, 2024 while the amending act is effective January 1, 2026 and the underlying regime originated in 2020; effective_date uses the operative date stated in the text. Section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms. Owner-type and tenancy-length conditions cannot be tested with building facts and are recorded as 'other' or 'owner_type' conditions.

rules.title: California statewide just-cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months (or 24 months if adult tenants were added), the owner may not terminate the tenancy without a just cause stated in the written notice. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver equal to one month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months' occupancy; relocation assistance = one month's rent
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.coverage_text: Covers residential rental tenancies in which the tenant has lived continuously and lawfully in the unit for 12 months (or 24 months in some cases with added adult tenants), in housing first issued a certificate of occupancy more than 15 years ago.

all_of.text: Housing that has not been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years
Tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months (or 24 months if additional adult tenants were added earlier)

exemptions.label: Single-family owner-occupied residence renting no more than two units or bedrooms

all_of.text: Single-family owner-occupied residence in which the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms
Two separate dwelling units within a single structure
Owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy

exemptions.label: Separately alienable property with natural-person owner and written exemption notice

all_of.value: natural person (not REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member)
all_of.text: Owner is not a real estate investment trust, a corporation, or an LLC in which at least one member is a corporation

all_of.value: alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit; tenants given written exemption notice
all_of.text: Property is alienable separate from the title to any other dwelling unit and tenants were given the required written exemption notice
Housing restricted as affordable for very low, low, or moderate income households or subject to a housing subsidy agreement

exemptions.label: Property subject to qualifying local just-cause ordinance

all_of.value: subject to local just-cause ordinance adopted on/before 2019-09-01 or more protective ordinance
all_of.text: Property is subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective local ordinance adopted or amended later

rules.exemptions_text: Exempts transient/tourist hotels, nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care and residential care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility housing with an owner, owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to two units or bedrooms, owner-occupied duplexes, mobilehome homeowners, housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, separately alienable property owned by a natural person with proper written notice, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, and property covered by a qualifying local just-cause ordinance.
rules.interaction: The section does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 applies, or where a more protective local ordinance adopted or amended later applies; a property cannot be subject to both. A less protective local ordinance adopted after September 1, 2019 is not enforced unless this section is repealed. Relocation assistance under this section is credited against relocation assistance required by other law.
yields_to: Local just-cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019
More protective local just-cause ordinances adopted or amended after September 1, 2019
